top_level_objectives: Identify the major structural components of DNA, including sugar-phosphate backbones and nitrogenous bases.
Explain antiparallel strand orientation and complementary base-pairing in the double helix.
Describe how helicase, single-strand binding proteins, DNA polymerase, and ligase function during DNA replication.
Distinguish leading- and lagging-strand synthesis and explain why DNA replication is semiconservative.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce DNA as a three-dimensional double helix and orient students to its overall architecture before examining details.
key_visuals: A large rotating DNA double helix
Two spiraling outer backbones
Base pairs bridging the interior
student_actions: Inspect the full helix from multiple angles
Identify the outer versus inner structural features
Describe the overall shape in relation to function

scenes.brief_purpose: Break one strand into its molecular components so students can recognize nucleotides and the sugar-phosphate backbone.
key_visuals: A single DNA strand enlarged
Repeated sugar-phosphate units
Attached bases labeled adenine, thymine, guanine, and cytosine
student_actions: Select or highlight sugars, phosphates, and bases
Trace how nucleotides connect along one strand
Match each base name to its structure or label

scenes.scene_name: Complementary Base Pairing in the Helix
scenes.brief_purpose: Show how bases project inward and pair specifically across the helix via hydrogen bonding.
key_visuals: Base pairs centered in the helix
A-T pairs with two hydrogen bonds
G-C pairs with three hydrogen bonds
student_actions: Compare A-T and G-C pairs
Count or identify hydrogen bonds in each pair
Predict the complementary base opposite a shown base

scenes.brief_purpose: Help students understand 5' to 3' and 3' to 5' orientation and how the two strands run in opposite directions.
key_visuals: Direction labels on both strands
One strand marked 5'→3'
Complementary strand marked 3'→5'
student_actions: Follow each backbone from one end to the other
Identify which ends are 5' and 3' on each strand
Explain what antiparallel means using the visual model

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the start of DNA replication by showing strand separation and stabilization of exposed templates.
key_visuals: A replication fork forming as the helix opens
Helicase at the fork
Single-strand binding proteins coating separated strands
student_actions: Observe how helicase separates the parental strands
Identify the role of single-strand binding proteins
Relate the opened strands to template use in replication

scenes.brief_purpose: Show how DNA polymerase synthesizes new DNA differently on the two templates because synthesis only proceeds 5' to 3'.
key_visuals: DNA polymerase on both template strands
Continuous synthesis on the leading strand
Discontinuous Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand
student_actions: Track the direction of polymerase movement and new strand growth
Distinguish leading versus lagging strand synthesis
Explain why Okazaki fragments are required on one side of the fork

scenes.brief_purpose: Conclude replication by joining fragments and showing the composition of the two daughter DNA molecules.
key_visuals: DNA ligase sealing gaps between Okazaki fragments
Two completed daughter double helices
Color contrast showing old versus newly synthesized strands
student_actions: Identify where ligase acts
Compare parental and daughter molecules
State why replication is called semiconservative
